concepts.def: Rock containing enough of a metal compound to make extraction worthwhile.
Metals less reactive than carbon (e.g. iron) are extracted by heating with coke in a blast furnace.
Tall furnace producing iron from iron oxide using coke, limestone and hot air.
Used for very reactive metals (Al, Na) because carbon can't reduce them.
Plants absorb metal ions; burning them gives an ash high in metal compounds.
Bacteria break down low-grade ores to give leachate solutions containing metal ions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Metals — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Metals brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Metals.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
